summary: A 1977 specification of NETRJS, a remote job entry protocol for sending batch jobs to a remote computer and getting results back. It replaced RFC 599 and is historic.

plainLanguage.summary: NETRJS lets a remote user submit batch jobs to UCLA's Remote Job Service and receive the resulting output. This RFC describes its console, data channels and transaction format.

subtitle: Describes remote batch-job submission to UCLA's RJS service over the ARPANET.

tldr.problem: Remote users needed to submit batch jobs to UCLA's Remote Job Service and receive print or punch output over the network.
tldr.mechanism: A Virtual Remote Batch Terminal uses a Telnet operator console and separate simplex data channels for card-reader, printer and punch streams.
tldr.outcome: RFC 740 is Historic and obsoletes RFCs 189 and 599.

today: The status of RFC 740 is Historic. It obsoletes RFC 189 and RFC 599.

sections.title: The Virtual Remote Batch Terminal
sections.content:
NETRJS is a private protocol defined and implemented by UCLA's Campus Computing Network for batch job submission to an IBM 360 Model 91. A remote NETRJS user process simulates a Virtual Remote Batch Terminal (VRBT).

A VRBT can include virtual card readers, printers and punches, as well as an operator console. The user sends card images and job control language; the service runs jobs and returns print or punch output to the VRBT that submitted them.
sections.plainLanguage: A remote process acts as a batch terminal. It sends job input to the service and receives the resulting printer or punch output.

sections.title: Connections and Session Setup
sections.content:
NETRJS uses a full-duplex Telnet connection for the operator console and separate simplex connections for card reader, printer and punch data. Data channels need to be open only while in use and may run sequentially or simultaneously.

A session starts with an ICP to a contact socket selected for the character set. After the server sends READY, the user sends a SIGNON terminal-id command. The server closes the console if a valid signon does not arrive within 3 minutes.
sections.plainLanguage: The console carries commands and status messages. Separate connections carry job input and output, and the session begins with a signon.

sections.title: Transactions and Job Data
sections.content:
Data channels carry logical records grouped into transactions preceded by headers. A transaction is limited to 880 8-bit bytes. Its header contains a sequence number and length, and each record begins with an op code that identifies the channel.

An End-of-Data transaction marks the end of a job or job stack. The RFC says error detection is limited to the op code and transaction sequence number; a data-transfer error aborts the entire transmission, with no restart provision in the protocol.
sections.plainLanguage: Data travels in numbered transactions, each containing records for one channel. End-of-Data marks the end, and a transfer error aborts the transmission.
